active_paradigms.idea: Replace COBYLA with a single analytic-Jacobian SLSQP solve of the epigraph formulation
active_paradigms.description: The current program begins from a 16-site triangular-lattice patch with three alternating corners removed, normalizes its diameter, and uses several noisy COBYLA runs to maximize a separation variable subject to all pair distances being between the separation and one. This is strong because the lattice patch has the correct dense-packing topology and COBYLA can deform it into the known near-optimal non-lattice arrangement. Its main weakness is that COBYLA is derivative-free, is given 240 highly redundant inequalities, and the returned point is renormalized after optimization, so its optimized auxiliary variable is not exactly the evaluated ratio. Instead, fix translation and rotation by setting point 0=(0,0) and point 1=(1,0), optimize the remaining 28 coordinates plus t, and impose d_ij^2-t >= 0 and 1-d_ij^2 >= 0 directly. Use one deterministic start from the current best lattice/deformed coordinates and provide explicit dense analytic Jacobians for every squared-distance constraint and for the objective -t. SLSQP's active-set QP steps are much better matched to the small set of tight contacts in this packing than COBYLA's linear interpolation model. Return the coordinates directly without a post-solve normalization, because the fixed unit-diameter pair already fixes scale. After the solve, evaluate the exact pdist score and only retain a result with a small strict feasibility margin in the upper-distance constraints.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Directly maximize t, which equals the evaluator's squared dmin/dmax ratio when the fixed pair remains a diameter pair. The target is to improve reliably beyond the approximately 0.077584 reference rather than merely exploiting COBYLA feasibility tolerance.
active_paradigms.cautions: Do not optimize dmin/dmax through min/max inside the objective; use t and smooth individual inequalities. Include all 120 pair constraints in both directions of the epigraph formulation, use float64 analytic gradients, and set ftol substantially below 1e-11. SLSQP can falsely report success at a slightly infeasible point, so verify all distances before returning and shrink coordinates infinitesimally toward the anchor if any non-anchor distance exceeds one.

active_paradigms.idea: Use deterministic differential evolution on an anchor-fixed, penalized global search formulation
active_paradigms.description: The current method has excellent local geometry but all of its starts belong to one narrow lattice basin, so it can miss a different contact graph whose true ratio is higher. Construct a globally parameterized formulation by fixing two presumed diameter endpoints at (0,0) and (1,0), leaving 14 free points, and bounding each free point to the intersection-relevant square [0,1] x [-0.5,0.5] or a safely larger unit-disk bounding box. Use scipy.optimize.differential_evolution once on a deterministic seed and a vectorized objective that returns negative minimum squared pair distance plus a very large smooth penalty for any pair with squared distance above one. The objective should explicitly include distances to the two fixed anchors and between every free pair. This directly targets the evaluator statistic rather than an auxiliary t, while the fixed anchors remove translation, rotation, and scale degeneracies that otherwise waste most of a population search. The optimizer can use a large population and Sobol initialization so that it tests contact topologies not reachable through tiny perturbations of the triangular patch. The best individual should be returned only after an exact distance check; if it has an upper-bound violation, radially contract all non-anchor points around the midpoint as a deterministic feasibility repair. This is a genuinely global alternative to the current local COBYLA basin search and is useful if the apparent reference configuration is not globally optimal.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Search for a higher-ratio contact topology and maximize the exact minimum squared distance while keeping the maximum distance at the anchored value one.
active_paradigms.cautions: A raw 28-dimensional global search is expensive, so use workers=1 for determinism, a fixed seed, vectorized population evaluation, and a finite evaluation budget appropriate for the evaluator timeout. The penalty must dominate any apparent gain in minimum distance from a diameter violation. The anchor assumption is valid up to relabeling whenever an optimal configuration has a diameter pair, but the chosen bounding box must not accidentally exclude geometrically valid points.

active_paradigms.idea: Freeze a high-precision contact-graph certificate as a static NumPy coordinate construction
active_paradigms.description: The evaluator has no requirement that optimization happen during evaluation: it imports the function and scores only the returned 16 by 2 array. The current program already spends runtime repeatedly solving a floating-point nonlinear program, then chooses whichever candidate has the best measured score; this introduces machine- and SciPy-version dependence and can lose score through final normalization. Use the current near-optimal output to identify its active contact graph offline, solve that fixed system to substantially higher precision outside the evaluated constructor, and store the resulting normalized coordinates as decimal float64 literals. The certificate should preserve every intended unit-diameter pair and give the shortest contacts a small positive clearance from accidental rounding changes. At runtime, the function should do only one numpy.asarray/numpy.array construction and return those immutable coordinates. This structural approach does not search for a new basin itself; its breakthrough value is that it converts any better solution found by a high-accuracy active-set solve into a deterministic, zero-optimization evaluator submission. It also permits systematic offline comparison of candidate contact graphs and choosing the one with the largest independently recomputed scipy.pdist ratio before freezing it. Because scoring is solely pairwise Euclidean distances, this static certificate is exactly equivalent to rerunning the optimizer but is far more numerically reproducible.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Numerical robustness and retention of the best attainable squared ratio: eliminate COBYLA termination error, random-start dependence, post-normalization drift, and runtime failure risk while preserving a verified ratio above the benchmark.
active_paradigms.cautions: Do not round coordinates aggressively: recompute all 120 float64 squared distances using the same SciPy/NumPy arithmetic expected by evaluation and retain at least 16 significant decimal digits. Ensure the stored set has exactly shape (16,2), dtype float64, no duplicated points, and no upper-distance violation caused by literal rounding. A static array only improves the score if the offline certificate is genuinely better than the current lattice-derived candidate; it is not a substitute for discovering that certificate.
